Zaïna: Arabic, feminine of Zain, meaning 'beauty' or 'adornment'.
Lizette: French diminutive of Elisabeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Haroon: Arabic and Urdu form of Aaron. Meaning uncertain, perhaps 'mountain of strength'.
Taym: Arabic Taym, meaning 'servant' or 'devotee'. Also a tribe name.
Junaid: Arabic Junayd, a diminutive of jund 'soldier' or 'warrior'.
Stans: Dutch short form of Constance or Stanislas, from Latin constans 'steadfast'.
Souhayb: Arabic Suhayb, a diminutive meaning 'reddish' or 'light-haired'. Name of a Companion.
Yamin: Arabic and Hebrew, meaning 'right hand' or 'right side'. Also Hebrew 'Benjamin'.
Lus: Probably a short form of Lucia, Luis or Lusine; Armenian Lus means 'light'. Origin uncertain.
Soe: Probably a Dutch short form or a Burmese name meaning 'storm' or 'lord'. Origin uncertain.
Loé: French variant of Chloé, from Greek 'green shoot', or a short form of Loïc.
Sol: Spanish and Latin for 'sun'. Also a Hebrew short form of Solomon.
Owais: Arabic Uways, a diminutive of aws 'gift' or 'wolf'. Name of the pious Uwais al-Qarani.
Zayden: Modern American coined name, from Zayd with -en added. Zayd is Arabic 'growth'.
Célice: Probably a French blend of Célia and Alice, or variant of Célis. Origin uncertain.
Milaya: Probably a modern variant of Milia or Milaya, from Slavic mil 'gracious' or 'dear'. Origin uncertain.
Toos: Dutch short form of Matthijs, or Antonius, from Hebrew 'gift of God' or a Roman family name.
Xander: Short form of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Nette: Short form of names ending in -nette, such as Annette or Antoinette. Also Dutch pet name.
Jannes: Dutch and German variant of Johannes, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Barbara: From Greek barbaros 'foreign, strange'. Saint Barbara is a Christian martyr.
Chris: Short form of Christopher, Christian or Christine, from Greek christos 'anointed'.
Francesca: Italian feminine of Francesco, from Latin Franciscus 'Frenchman' or 'free man'.
Alycia: Variant of Alicia, from Germanic Adalheidis 'noble kind'.
Ricardo: Spanish and Portuguese form of Richard, from Germanic ric 'ruler' and hard 'brave'.
Annaëlle: French blend of Anna and Elle, with Hebrew roots 'grace' and 'God'. Modern coined name.
Meriem: Arabic and French North African form of Mary, from Hebrew Miryam, meaning uncertain.
Eray: Turkish, from er 'man' or 'brave' and ay 'moon'. Means 'brave moon' or 'moon man'.
Joana: Portuguese and Catalan form of Joanna, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Maverick: English, from the Texan rancher Samuel Maverick, whose name came to mean an independent person.
Stanislas: French form of Slavic Stanislav, from stani 'become' and slava 'glory'.
Lloyd: Welsh, from llwyd 'grey'. Originally a nickname for someone with grey hair.
Aleksandra: Slavic form of Alexandra, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Divine: English word name from Latin divinus 'of a god'. Also used as a girls' name in Africa and the Caribbean.
Aimy: Variant of Amy or Aimée, from French 'beloved'. Probably a modern spelling.
Maram: Arabic, meaning 'wish' or 'aim'. Also used in Syria and Lebanon.
Dani: Short form of Daniel or Daniela, from Hebrew 'God is my judge'.
Vita: Latin for 'life'. Used in Italian and Latvian use.
Lilly-Rose: Compound of Lilly (flower, or short form of Elizabeth) and Rose, from Germanic 'fame' or Latin rosa.
Maoro: Italian and Spanish variant of Mauro, from Latin Maurus 'dark-skinned' or 'Moor'.
Elma: Short form of Wilhelmina, or from Germanic 'divine protection'. Also Arabic and Turkish uses.
Toine: Dutch and Flemish short form of Antonius, a Roman family name of uncertain meaning.
Feliz: Spanish, from Latin felix 'happy, lucky'. Also a Filipino variant of Felix.
Alvin: English, from Old English Ælfwine, 'elf friend'. Also a German variant of Alwin.
Ata: Turkish, meaning 'ancestor'. Also Arabic for 'gift' and used in Ghana and Tonga.
Devran: Turkish, meaning 'era' or 'age', from Arabic dawran.
Léanne: French variant of Leanne, a blend of Lee and Anne, possibly from Gaelic. Modern coinage.
Kristian: Scandinavian and Dutch form of Christian, from Latin christianus 'follower of Christ'.
Ayron: Modern variant of Aaron, from Hebrew, meaning uncertain, perhaps 'mountain of strength'.
Aliana: Modern coined name, possibly a variant of Alianna or Aliyana. Origin uncertain.
Lennox: Scottish, from the district Lennox, from Gaelic leamhanach 'place of elms'.
Liliane: French, from Lily or Lilian, possibly from Latin lilium 'lily'.
Juliann: Variant of Julian or Julianne, from Latin Julianus, 'of Julius'. Meaning uncertain, perhaps 'youthful'.
Cylia: Probably a variant of Célia or Cylia, from Latin caelum 'heaven'. Origin uncertain.
Rowen: English, from the rowan tree, or a variant of Irish Ruadhán 'red-haired'.
Noëlla: Feminine form of Noël, from Latin natalis 'birth', meaning Christmas.
Ezechiel: French and Dutch form of Ezekiel, from Hebrew 'God strengthens'.
Agata: Italian and Polish form of Agatha, from Greek agathe 'good'.
Aliou: West African form of Ali, from Arabic 'high' or 'exalted'.
Rosan: Dutch, a blend of Rosa and Ann, or from Persian roshan 'bright'.
Sanna: Finnish and Swedish short form of Susanna, from Hebrew 'lily'. Also Arabic 'brilliance'.
Yahia: Arabic form of John, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'. The Quranic prophet Yahya.
Maïsha: Swahili for 'life', also used as a variant of Aisha in Arabic and French.
Hadassa: Hebrew Hadassah, meaning 'myrtle'. The Hebrew name of Queen Esther.
Mimi: Italian and French pet name for Maria or Miriam. Also Japanese mimi 'ear'.
Ace: English, from Latin as 'one' via playing cards; implies the best. Also a short form of Horace.
Ayub: Arabic form of Job, from Hebrew Iyyov, perhaps 'persecuted' or 'repentant'.
Joah: Probably a variant of Joah, a Hebrew biblical name meaning 'Yahweh is brother', or a modern spelling of Joa. Origin uncertain.
Raffaella: Italian feminine of Raffaello, from Hebrew 'God has healed'.
Liona: Feminine form of Leon or Lion, from Greek leon 'lion'.
Menzo: Frisian and Dutch short form of Hermen or Meinhard. From Germanic 'strong' and 'brave'.
Ivanna: Slavic feminine of Ivan, the form of John, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Oria: Probably Latin or Italian, from aureus 'golden', or a variant of Oriah. Origin uncertain.
Wilma: German short form of Wilhelmina, from Germanic wil 'will' and helm 'helmet'.
Billie-Rose: Compound of Billie, a nickname from William ('resolute protector'), and Rose.
Loujain: Arabic, meaning 'silver'. Also used in Gulf countries.
Maë: Breton and French short form, possibly from Maël 'prince', or Mae, a variant of May.
Randa: Arabic, meaning 'fragrant tree' or 'laurel', or a scented plant.
Nuh: Arabic and Turkish form of Noah, from Hebrew 'rest'.
Élina: French form of Elina, from Greek Helene 'torch' or Finnish form of Helen.
Iasmina: Romanian and Greek variant of Jasmine, from Persian yasmin, a flower name.
Fos: Dutch short form of Foskes or Foss, perhaps from Latin fossa or a Frisian pet name. Origin uncertain.
Göktu: Turkish, from gök 'sky' with tu. Probably a modern name; origin uncertain.
Norélie: Modern French coined name, probably blending Nora and Aurélie. Origin uncertain.
Niaz: Persian and Urdu, meaning 'need' or 'supplication', also 'desire'.
Roa: Probably a short form or variant of Rowa or Roya, or a Finnish name. Origin uncertain.
Mayan: Hebrew ma'yan 'spring' or 'fountain'. Also refers to the Maya civilisation.
Serafim: Slavic and Portuguese form of Seraphim, from Hebrew seraphim 'fiery ones'.
Manël: Breton form of Manuel, from Hebrew Immanuel 'God is with us'.
Thiam: West African surname, used as a given name, from Wolof. Origin uncertain.
Ellana: Modern English name, probably a blend of Ella and Ana. Also Tolkienesque. Origin uncertain.
Amayah: Modern variant of Amaya, a Basque name 'the end', or Japanese 'night rain'.
Maksym: Ukrainian form of Maxim, from Latin maximus 'greatest'.
Solomia: Ukrainian form of Salome, from Hebrew shalom 'peace'.
Louèn: Breton, probably a variant of Louen, a Breton saint's name meaning 'joyful'. Origin uncertain.
Meau: Probably a French or Thai-inspired coined name, or a Vietnamese variant. Origin uncertain.
Omèr: Hebrew Omer, meaning 'sheaf of grain'. Also Arabic Umar, 'long-lived'.
Devin: Irish Gaelic Dáibhéid or Damhán, 'poet'. Also a variant of Devon.
Arinas: Lithuanian male name, possibly from Latin Arinus. Origin uncertain.
Lysio: Modern name, perhaps from Greek lysis 'release' or Lysias. Origin uncertain.
Quentin: French, from Latin Quintinus, a diminutive of Quintus 'fifth'.
Kelly: Irish, from Ceallach 'bright-headed' or 'strife'. Also used as a girls' name.
Damien: French form of Damian, from Greek damazo 'to tame' or 'subdue'.
Jennifer: Cornish form of Guinevere, from Welsh 'white wave' or 'fair and smooth'.
Laurine: French feminine of Laurent, from Latin Laurentius, 'from Laurentum' or 'laurel'.
Stephanie: French and German feminine of Stephen, from Greek stephanos 'crown'.
Ludovic: French form of Ludovicus, from Germanic hlud 'famous' and wig 'warrior'.
Valerie: French form of Valeria, from Latin valere 'to be strong'.
Nienke: Dutch and Frisian pet form of names like Catharina or Nina. Meaning from those names.
Hicham: Arabic Hisham, meaning 'generosity' or 'crushing'. Name of Umayyad caliphs.
Emmanuelle: French feminine of Emmanuel, from Hebrew 'God is with us'.
Rabia: Arabic, meaning 'spring' or 'fourth'. Also Turkish form Rabia.
Emely: Modern variant of Emily, from Latin Aemilia, a Roman family name, possibly from aemulus 'rival'.
Hasse: Scandinavian short form of Hans or Hasse, or Dutch pet form. From John 'God is gracious'.
Mette: Danish and Norwegian short form of Margrethe, from Greek margarites 'pearl'. Also a short form of Mathilde.
Danaé: French form of Danae, mother of Perseus in Greek myth. Possibly from Greek 'parched'.
Devon: English, from the county of Devon, from Celtic Dumnonii, perhaps 'deep valley dwellers'.
Monica: Latin and Italian, possibly from Greek monos 'alone' or an African name. Mother of Saint Augustine.
Diégo: French spelling of Spanish Diego, probably from Santiago, or Greek didache 'teaching'.
Denzel: Cornish, from a place name, possibly 'stronghold'. Popularised by the actor Denzel Washington.
Gianluca: Italian compound of Gian (from Giovanni) and Luca, from Hebrew 'God is gracious' and Greek Loukas 'from Lucania'.
Flavia: Latin, feminine of Flavius, from flavus 'golden' or 'blond'.
Germain: French, from Latin Germanus 'brother' or 'of the same stock'. Also 'from Germany'.
Amaryllis: Greek, from amarysso 'to sparkle'. A shepherdess in classical pastoral poetry, and the flower.
Alexa: Short form of Alexandra, from Greek alexo 'defend' and aner 'man'.
Rayen: Mapuche 'flower'. Also an Arabic, French and Spanish variant of Rayan. Origin varies.
Skye: Scottish, from the Isle of Skye, perhaps from Old Norse 'cloud island'.
Hubert: Germanic, from hug 'mind' and beraht 'bright'. Saint Hubert is the patron of hunters.
Nessa: Irish short form of Agnes or Vanessa, or Irish 'not gentle'. Also Hebrew 'miracle'.
Belinay: Turkish, a blend of Belin 'ebony' and ay 'moon'. Modern Turkish name.
Waël: Arabic Wa'il, meaning 'one who seeks refuge' or 'returning'.
Mariana: Spanish and Portuguese combination of Maria and Ana, from Hebrew 'beloved' and 'grace'.
Sixtine: French feminine of Sixtus, from Latin sextus 'sixth'.
Freek: Dutch short form of Frederik, from Germanic 'peaceful ruler'.
Alexandro: Spanish and Italian-influenced form of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Emmelie: Modern variant of Emily, or a blend of Emma and Amélie. From Latin Aemilia.
Marguerite: French form of Margaret, from Greek margarites 'pearl'. Also the daisy flower.
Free: Dutch short form of Frederika or Free, from Germanic 'peaceful ruler'. Also English 'free'.
Lin: Chinese 'forest', or short form of Linda or Linus. Meaning depends on the origin.
Vital: French and Portuguese, from Latin vitalis 'of life', from vita.
Moira: Irish form of Mary, or Greek moira 'fate'. Scottish and Irish name.
Souhaib: Arabic Suhayb, meaning 'reddish' or 'light-haired'. Companion of the Prophet.
Eros: Greek, meaning 'love' or 'desire'. The god of love in Greek mythology.
Wilson: English, meaning 'son of William', from Germanic 'resolute protector'.
Ries: Dutch short form of Marinus or Hendrik, with pet form from Marius, or Hendries. Origin partly uncertain.
Lonne: Dutch, a variant of Lonne or Lone, from Loes or Leonora. Origin uncertain.
Heidi: Swiss German, short form of Adelheid, from Germanic 'noble kind'. Famous from Johanna Spyri's novel.
Kamilia: Variant of Camilla, from a Roman family name, possibly 'attendant at a sacrifice'. Also Arabic Kamilah 'perfect'.
Aïssata: West African form of Aisha, from Arabic 'alive' or 'well-living'.
Ivo: Germanic, from iv 'yew'. Also a Slavic form of Ivan.
Eya: Arabic, meaning 'life' or Tunisian variant of Aya 'sign, verse'.
Nuno: Portuguese, possibly from Latin nonus 'ninth' or Germanic 'noon'. Origin uncertain.
Warren: English, from a Norman surname meaning 'game park' or Germanic 'guard'.
Elana: Hebrew 'tree' or variant of Eliana or Helena. From Hebrew ilan 'tree'.
Simeon: Hebrew Shimon, meaning 'he has heard'. A son of Jacob in the Bible.
Annette: French diminutive of Anne, from Hebrew 'grace'.
Jools: Short form of Julia or Julian, or English nickname for Jules. From Roman Julius.
Ylona: Variant of Ilona, a Hungarian form of Helen, from Greek 'torch'.
Mories: Dutch variant of Maurits or Mories, from Latin Mauritius, 'dark-skinned'.
Maksymilian: Polish form of Maximilian, from Latin Maximilianus, a blend of Maximus and Aemilianus.
Maryem: Variant of Maryam, the Arabic form of Mary, from Hebrew Miryam.
Heaven: English word name for the sky or paradise. Modern given name since the 20th century.
Shelby: English, from an Old English place name 'willow farm' or surname.
Zian: Probably a modern variant of Zayn or Ziyan; also Chinese 'Zi An'. Origin uncertain.
Milly: English pet form of Millicent or Emily. From Germanic 'strength' or Latin Aemilia.
Ajan: Possibly a Somali, Hungarian or Arabic name. Meaning varies; origin uncertain.
Séraphin: French form of Seraphim, from Hebrew seraphim, 'burning ones'.
Roxan: Variant of Roxana, from Persian raushanak 'bright' or 'dawn'.
Nana: Many origins: Ghanaian Akan 'king' or 'elder', Greek, Georgian, and Japanese. Also a children's pet name for a grandmother.
Aboubakr: French spelling of Abu Bakr, 'father of the young camel'. Name of the first caliph.
Shimon: Hebrew form of Simeon, meaning 'he has heard'.
Emilian: Romanian and Slavic form of Aemilianus, from the Roman family name Aemilius.
Cheikh: French spelling of Arabic Shaykh, 'elder' or 'leader'. Common in West Africa.
Mihai: Romanian form of Michael, from Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Isidore: French form of Isidorus, from Greek 'gift of Isis'.
Manolo: Spanish pet form of Manuel, from Hebrew Immanuel 'God is with us'.
Rui: Portuguese short form of Rodrigo, from Germanic 'famous ruler'. Also Chinese and Japanese names.
Jared: Hebrew Yered, 'descent' or 'rose'. A biblical patriarch.
Manelle: Modern French and Arabic variant of Manel, from Arabic manal 'attainment'.
Tove: Scandinavian, from Old Norse Tófa, a short form of Thorfrid, 'Thor's peace'.
Kaja: Polish and Estonian short form of Katarzyna, from Greek 'pure'. Also Slovenian Kaja.
Ruíz: Spanish surname, from Ruy, a short form of Rodrigo, used as a given name. 'Famous ruler'.
Tayler: Variant of Taylor, an English occupational surname meaning 'tailor'.
